articles.title: Gold falls 11% to Rs 1.21 lakh and silver plunges 16.2% to Rs 1.47 lakh in a week to over one-year lows; analysts warn prices may slide further as US inflation data and Federal Reserve rate signals shape outlook
articles.summary: Gold price crash to continue?
articles.body: Gold price crash to continue? Gold and silver prices could face further selling pressure next week after both metals slumped to their lowest levels in more than a year. Analysts have said that investors will watch US inflation figures and signals from the Federal Reserve for indications of where interest rates are headed.Markets will also track mid-month purchasing managers’ index (PMI) readings from major economies, followed by US gross domestic product (GDP) figures, housing market data and durable goods orders. Inflation data will be particularly important in determining expectations about the Fed’s monetary policy, analysts said.Gold and silver prices crashOn the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), December gold futures shed Rs 14,927, or 11%, over the past week, settling at Rs 1,21,778 per 10 grams. The contract touched a low not seen in more than a year.Gold was last traded at a comparable level on October 30, 2025, when its price stood at Rs 1,21,508 per 10 grams, according to a PTI report.Silver futures for December delivery recorded a steeper weekly decline, losing Rs 28,496, or 16.2%, and also falling to a more than one-year low. The metal was last quoted near these levels on November 3, 2025, at Rs 1,47,758 per kg.The downturn in precious metals was equally pronounced in overseas markets. Comex gold futures lost $370.9, or 9.5%, during the week, ending at $3,515.4 per ounce. Silver futures fared worse, dropping $8.05, or 16.4%, to settle at $41.07 per ounce.Gold, silver price outlookPranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG -- Commodity & Currency Research at JM Financial Services Ltd, said the outlook for both precious metals remained subdued, with the ongoing decline likely to continue. The widespread decline in artificial intelligence-linked stocks has added to the selling pressure.Silver has also been hit by weakness across the industrial metals segment, with copper and zinc recording particularly sharp declines, Mer pointed out.According to him, the sell-off in equities prompted investors to liquidate bullion holdings as well, while demand for safe-haven bonds increased.The US dollar continued to hold firm, moving towards the 104 level against a basket of major currencies. articles.summary: The rupee snapped its five-session winning streak on Monday after touching a seven-month high, as corporate demand for dollars and weakness in domestic
articles.body: The rupee snapped its five-session winning streak on Monday after touching a seven-month high, as corporate demand for dollars and weakness in domestic equities offset support from strong foreign portfolio inflows.The currency climbed to around 92.43-92.44 against the US dollar in early trade, its strongest level since April, before reversing direction. It was trading at 92.85 in early trade, down 23 paise from its previous close, according to PTI. Reuters later quoted the rupee at 92.8825, compared with its previous close of 92.67.The retreat came after a sharp rally over the past week. The rupee had gained 70 paise on Friday to close at 92.62, moving above the 93 mark for the first time since April 10. It had strengthened more than 1.6% over five consecutive sessions from its November 13 close of 94.19.The currency's recovery has been supported by strong foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities. Overseas investors have poured about $13 billion into domestic stocks so far in November, according to Reuters, amid a global rotation away from crowded artificial intelligence trades.However, traders said a burst of corporate dollar buying weighed on the rupee after its early gains, with demand reportedly coming from two large conglomerates. The currency's rapid appreciation had also pushed it into overbought territory, according to a key momentum indicator.Goldman Sachs described the rupee as a “port of stability in the AI storm”, saying the currency had benefited from the broader shift in global market positioning.The brokerage, however, cautioned that the pace of appreciation may not be sustainable, given India's need to rebuild its external reserve buffers. It said there appeared to be a greater willingness to allow two-way volatility in the currency.India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.205 billion to $705.342 billion in the week ended November 13, according to Reserve Bank of India data, taking them to a three-month low.The dollar index was down 0.03% at 103.71, while Brent crude futures fell 0.28% to $92.38 a barrel.Domestic equities were lower in early trade, with the Sensex falling 0.49% and the Nifty declining 0.46%. Foreign institutional investors had bought equities worth Rs 10,308.42 crore on a net basis on Friday, according to exchange data.The rupee has also strengthened against other major currencies in November, gaining around 4% against the British pound and the euro and 3% against the Japanese yen, Reuters reported.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: Stock market crash today: Amid the ongoing record rally, Indian equity benchmarks snapped their winning streak to crash in trade on Monday. BSE Sensex and Nifty50 both plunged over 1.5% as profit booking and global cues led to a slide.Weakness also spread to the broader market, with the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices slipping into negative territory.BSE Sensex ended the day at 82,435.99, down 1,4584 points or 1.77%. Nifty50 closed at 25,349.65, down 451 points or 1.75%. The crash wiped out over Rs 6.39 lakh crore of investors’ wealth, with market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies dropping to Rs 508 lakh crore.Among Sensex constituents, Tata Steel, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI) and UltraTech Cement dropped by as much as 6%. In contrast, TCS, Tech Mahindra, Infosys, HCL Tech and Maruti Suzuki were among the stocks trading higher.Why did stock market crash today? Top reasons1) Profit booking after a sharp rallyThe biggest reason is profit booking that has emerged after the recent record breaking run of stocks. Nifty has gained more than 10% and is on course to deliver its best monthly performance since 2020, prompting investors to lock in gains after the sharp rise.Indian equities are approaching their previous record highs, supported by a turnaround in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows that has significantly altered market sentiment. The Nifty 50 is now just over 2% below its lifetime high of 26,373.20, while the Sensex is less than 3% away from its record peak of 86,159.2) Concerns over a US Fed rate hike resurfaceExpectations of tighter US monetary policy have returned to the forefront, with markets assigning a 93% probability to an interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool.The Fed's interest rate outlook also remains an important driver of bullion prices. On Friday, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook supported further rate increases, arguing that the prevailing policy rate was not high enough to tackle inflation, which she said she viewed with "great concern".A rate increase by the US central bank can make American investments more attractive relative to Indian equities.3) Rupee depreciation adds to market concernsThe Indian rupee weakened sharply and was heading towards the 93-per-dollar level after briefly moving above 92.50. The currency had closed at 92.67 on Friday.A weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of imports, particularly crude oil, increasing expenses for Indian businesses and adding to inflationary pressures. It can also erode the dollar-denominated returns earned by overseas investors, making Indian equities less attractive and potentially prompting further FPI selling.4) Selling in heavyweight stocks weighs on indicesSeveral of the market's biggest constituents, including HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI) and Axis Bank, declined by as much as 2.5% on Monday, adding to the pressure on benchmark indices.The impact of these declines on the Nifty is amplified by the index's market capitalisation-based weighting system.Stock market outlookVinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited says, “Last week’s late global sell-off, triggered by concerns over an AI bubble and tighter US monetary policy, weighed on Indian equities today. Selling was concentrated in heavyweight banking and commodity stocks amid weak FII sentiment. The domestic market also remains vulnerable to profit booking after the recent sharp rally and a holiday-shortened week. Mixed Asian markets and a positive European opening helped limit losses. The outlook hinges on whether the AI-led sell-off remains contained. Although valuations have corrected significantly, concerns over the sustainability of debt-funded data-centre investments continue to weigh on global sentiment. Further weakness in global equities could spill over into India, though the impact may be relatively limited given India’s lower exposure to AI-driven investment and resilient domestic economy. Improving manufacturing activity and expectations of robust Q2 GDP growth of ~7.7% remain key fundamental supports for a constructive medium- to long-term outlook."(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Artificial superintelligence ‘arriving’, warns top Meta executive
articles.summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang says humankind’s actions over next year will have ‘great consequence’ for the world.
articles.body:
Meta’s top AI executive has sounded the alarm about the risk of humanity losing control of AI, warning that superintelligence that far exceeds the human intellect is imminent.

Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang issued the warning on Sunday after an employee at AI giant Anthropic announced that he had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.

Wang said the breakthrough dwarfed any human achievement for “sheer intellectual might”.

The 29-year-old executive said the milestone showed that emerging AI models will be “clearly superhuman” at improving themselves, as well as “massively accelerating” research in fields such as biology, armaments and economics.

“Superintelligence is arriving,” Wang said on X.

“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in.”

Wang, who co-founded Scale AI before joining Meta as the tech giant’s first chief AI officer last year, said it is unlikely humankind will be able to control AI that achieves unconstrained recursive self-improvement or is “1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”

“Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully,” Wang said.

AI safety advocates have identified recursive self-improvement – where AI models become capable of advancing without human input – as a critical tipping point after which humanity could lose the ability to control the technology.

While the risks of frontier AI have stoked intense debate in Silicon Valley, there is no consensus on how to maximise the benefits of the technology without exposing humanity to catastrophic risks.

Meta has largely positioned itself on the more optimistic side of the debate, with CEO and cofounder Mark Zuckerberg rejecting calls by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for a coordinated slowdown in development to beef up guardrails.

In an essay published in August, Zuckerberg lamented that discussions about AI were “filled with doom” and said the technology should lead to “more people sharing greater prosperity, health and freedom.”

In his post on Sunday, Wang criticised “lazy thinking” within the AI industry that he said treated superintelligence as inevitable.

“We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI. We should endeavour ourselves to build a technology which delivers a positive future for humanity, where all humans have greater agency and empowerment,” Wang said.

“I strongly believe this is possible, but likely involves the whole industry taking meaningfully different actions from the “default path” in front of us.”

articles.title: She bought her new home at a great price. Then cracks started to appear
articles.summary: Brette Abshier didn’t pay much attention when a crack formed in her living room tile last year. But it was just the beginning of what seemed like a much deeper problem.
articles.body: Brette Abshier didn’t pay much attention when a crack formed in her living room tile last year. But it was just the beginning of what seemed like a much deeper problem. A few months ago, she said, the small crack began growing — and quickly. It began extending across the entire house. Soon, she could see the crack from the outside of the foundation. Cracks started appearing on the walls, then the ceiling, then the exterior stucco. Nails in her home started popping outward. Some cracks in a concrete foundation are common as new construction settles into the soil, and Lennar, the construction company that built Abshier’s house, had said her home’s foundation is still within tolerance levels. Abshier bought her home in 2019. Still, she took to social media. “This morning my builder came to check on my house and told me that the crack from one side of my house to the other side of my house is completely normal,” she posted on TikTok in September. “I wanna know if this is normal and other people are experiencing this, because I don’t think this is normal.” Abshier has posted about a dozen videos documenting the issues with her home in Austin, Texas. The videos have amassed hundreds of thousands of views, with one gaining more than 1.2 million views. In the United States, a longstanding trend began reversing over the past couple of years: newly built homes are now selling for less than pre-owned ones. The median price of a new home was $400,400 in September, according to the US Census Bureau, compared with $417,500 for an existing home, per the National Association of Realtors. With record-high home prices and elevated borrowing costs, many cost-conscious buyers are drawn to the price tag of newly built homes. To sweeten the deal, the nation’s largest builders increasingly offer smaller and cheaper floor plans as well as incentives such as closing-cost assistance and mortgage-rate buydowns. But US homebuilders are also being dogged by claims of shoddy workmanship. Lawsuits against major homebuilders are on the rise, said a legal expert, and viral social media posts like Abshier’s warn of the headaches that can come with new construction. “The more I look at the damage that’s slowly getting worse and worse, the bigger of a project I see coming,” Abshier told CNN. “It’s not just fixing the foundation and laying new floor down at this point. It’s in almost every single room that I’ve got something going on.” In a statement, Lennar said it stands behind its homes. “Every new Lennar home is backed by our 1-2-10 limited warranty: one year on workmanship, two years on systems, and 10 years on structural elements,” a Lennar spokesperson said. “We are in contact with the homeowners who have shared concerns with us, and we are working with them to review and address each situation.” Growing pains Abshier said she was proud to become a homeowner in her 20s. She bought the newly built three-bedroom home for about $440,000, with Lennar covering closing costs and connecting her with a lender. She said her total upfront cost was less than $10,000. Newly constructed homes have increasingly been built in areas with cheaper land values, which has kept prices lower, said Robert Dietz, chief economist at the National Association of Home Builders. Relatively inexpensive land and fewer regulatory hurdles have helped fuel construction in some markets. Sun Belt states, including Texas and Florida, have been among the nation’s most active homebuilding markets in recent years, even as the United States faces a housing shortage. But in the drive to expand housing supply, mistakes can be made, said Jordan Van Voorst, a home inspector who works in Florida and Alabama. Van Voorst said he suspects the pressure to ramp up construction, coupled with a shortage of construction workers, may sometimes come at the expense of quality. Since moving from Colorado to the South a few years ago, Van Voorst said he’s been flagging quality issues in new construction far more often than he did in his previous market. “Half of the inspection, you just go around your house and start shaking things, and you’ll be amazed at how much stuff is loose. Loose light fixtures, loose kitchen islands, loose mirrors,” Van Voorst said. Most of the issues he finds in new constructions can be easily repaired, but first-time home buyers may be particularly vulnerable to problems because they don’t know what to look for, he said. New construction can also have perks, though. New homes are often more energy-efficient than older homes, and the builder is supposed to fix any issues as long as the home is still under warranty. This makes inspections easier for Van Voorst, too: “I say, ‘Hey, these are the things that are wrong,’ and the builder usually fixes everything I find,” he said. ‘Do I regret this house?’ About 250 miles north of Austin, in the Dallas suburb of Celina, Texas, Brad Crabtree’s home looks like it’s splitting open. A massive fissure has opened along the side of his home, breaking apart the brickwork and exposing the layers beneath. Cracked tiles inside the home have left sharp edges, forcing his children to watch where they walk. More than once, they’ve cut their feet, he said. “Every time it rains, I lie awake hearing the rain hit the side of the house where there’s a big old gap, thinking, ‘Boy, I hope this doesn’t create an additional problem for me,’” he added. A CNN search of complaints shows lawsuits filed in the past few years against the nation’s largest homebuilders by homeowners alleging faulty workmanship and builders cutting corners. Ian Faria, an attorney in Texas who represents homebuilders, said lawsuits have increased in recent years in part because of newer building codes. The newer guidelines require homes to have fewer air gaps than in previous decades. As a result, “if any one thing goes wrong, it can become a bigger problem than it needs to be,” Faria said. But Faria said he has also seen major builders pulled into costly lawsuits over what he considers baseless claims of mold or building code violations. That means builders need to set aside more money for legal liabilities, adding to overall building costs. “All they’re doing is increasing costs for builders they ultimately will have to pass onto the consumer,” Faria said. “So houses will cost more. It’s a shame.” Like Abshier’s home, Crabtree’s, which he purchased in 2021, was built by Lennar. Both are still under the company’s 10-year structural warranty. The difference: In late September, Lennar agreed to fix Crabtree’s home after months of back and forth. “Do I regret the house? Our kids have enjoyed growing up here, but we probably would have asked more questions,” he said. “Or knowing what we know now, maybe bought somewhere else.” Neither Crabtree nor Abshier said they plan to take legal action — at least for now. Abshier said she has been in steady communication with Lennar recently. “There are a lot of people in my life telling me I’m being a little bit too optimistic right now,” Abshier said. “But I’m hopeful the builder will do the right thing.”

A detail of Brette Abshier's Austin, Texas, home in November 2026. Some cracks in a concrete foundation are common as new construction settles into the soil.

"A lot of the changes I'm seeing right now are on the exterior of the house," Brette Abshier said. Her home now has cracks on both the inside and outside. "I'm starting to get horizontal cracking in my stucco."
Brette Abshier, 33, sitting in front of her home. Abshier was proud to become a homeowner when she moved into the home in 2019.

As the cracks grew, Brette Abshier began marking her walls and floors with Sharpie to keep track. "Every day I'd look, and it would look so much worse," she said. "I know it's gonna have to be fixed anyways.”
Workers fill dirt into an irrigation trench for a home under construction by Lennar Homes in Vacaville, California, on July 14, 2026.

When Brad Crabtree first noticed the brick on the exterior of his Celina, Texas home splitting, he chalked it up to normal settling that happens with new construction. In September, Lennar agreed to repair the home after inspecting it and deeming the foundation cracks beyond what is "in tolerance," Crabtree said.

Floor cracks in Brad Crabtree's home in September 2026. After initial inspections by Lennar earlier this year characterized the home's cracks as cosmetic rather than structural, Crabtree said he hired an independent inspector.

Before the builder agreed to repair Brad Crabtree's home, he said he "began to lose hope." "I'm literally watching my house split apart. I have photos showing different times of the year, and you could literally see the brickwork separating," he said.

articles.title: War against data centers is costing local communities millions of dollars
articles.summary: A blocked $5 billion data center at Landover Mall could have helped cut Prince George's County's $130 million deficit, as vacant lots could fund schools and roads.
articles.body: Affordability and data centers were on the ballot this November. Voters made it clear that they are concerned about both issues: prices are too high and the neighborliness of data centers is in doubt. In a time of economic turbulence, cities and counties are struggling to pay for schools, roads and public safety without the tax revenue data centers generate. Where can part of the solution to affordability and concerns with data centers be found? Vacant lots. Vacant lots can host data centers that are well maintained, comply with local architectural requirements, have security and bring in much-needed cash for local projects. An eyesore and security problem can become a revenue generator and a secure property. However, some are determined to keep data centers from developing the local economy and unsightly properties at any cost. In early November, an activist helped block the development of a $5 billion data center that was set to break ground in the next year or so. The data center was supposed to be built on the site of Landover Mall, which closed in 2002. The vacant lot is now overgrown with grass and weeds, stretching across nearly 90 acres in Landover, Md. AMERICA'S REDDEST STATE CHASES BILLION-DOLLAR BOOM AS OTHERS SOUR ON MASSIVE EMERGING INDUSTRY Prince George's County, home to the former mall, is facing a $130 million budget deficit. It has lost a Six Flags amusement park, is losing the Washington Commanders to Washington, D.C., and has suffered thousands of federal job losses. Developers projected about $53.5 million a year in local tax revenue if the data center were to be built. The activist, Taylor Frazier McCollum, isn't moved by those numbers or how they help her neighbors. "Money is, you know, a made-up concept," she said. "We buy into it every day, and we choose that this has value and this doesn't have value and to me the environment has the highest and utmost value and I need to honor that in any way." INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE' The rejection of a project to help revitalize a site that sorely needs it and fill the county's coffers perfectly encapsulates the political debate around data centers. Too often, proposed data centers receive automatic opposition from activists and politicians. As a result, some of America's most vulnerable and desperate communities are losing millions of dollars in tax revenue that could fund schools, fix roads, pay emergency responders and more. Landover Mall is sadly not the only example. Local opposition blocked or delayed at least 75 data center projects across the country worth approximately $130 billion in the first quarter of 2026, which Data Center Watch describes as the largest single-quarter total on record. That's roughly as much as all of 2025, in just three months. HOW AMERICA CAN WIN THE AI RACE WITHOUT BURNING VOTERS In Virginia, Prince William County stands to miss out on as much as $400 million in projected annual tax revenue following the collapse of Digital Gateway, once billed as one of the largest data center complexes in the world. The county had approved the project, but courts invalidated its rezoning approvals. The remaining developer withdrew its legal challenge in July 2026, effectively ending the plans. On the other hand, communities that are looking to the future and allowing data centers are reaping the benefits. Virginia’s Loudoun County has embraced data centers, which have generated 38% of general fund revenue in the county’s FY2026 budget. That revenue has helped the county lower its real property tax rate every year for a decade, from $1.145 per $100 of assessed value in 2016 to $0.805 in 2026. That's real money back in homeowners' pockets. That is revenue its neighbor, Prince William County, is missing out on. HOMEOWNERS IN THE HEART OF AMERICA’S AI BOOM ARE GETTING AN UNEXPECTED PAYOFF In Henrico County, Virginia, data center tax revenue pays for an Affordable Housing Trust Fund that helps first-time homebuyers with down payments. A single mother working toward a nursing degree said her new mortgage costs less than her old rent. In Richland Parish, Louisiana, Meta's data center expansion helped the parish pay for $50,000 in teacher bonuses. THE POWERFUL WAY AMERICAN COMMUNITIES CAN BENEFIT FROM THE NEW TECH BOOM REVEALED BY DATA CENTER CEO Data center developers have a responsibility to communities: listen to their concerns, be transparent and collaborative about their plans, design in ways their neighbors approve and work to mitigate or eliminate undesirable local impacts. They must also pay their own electric and water costs, establish noise limits and continually work with local community groups and elected officials to address concerns as they arise. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Data center development can be and often is a win-win for developers and the community. But even these efforts are not enough for some. Money may be a "made-up concept" to some, but the lower tax rates in Loudoun County, the down payment in Henrico and the teacher bonuses in Richland Parish are real. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Data centers can turn a decades-long vacant parking lot overgrown with weeds into an economic engine, helping to close a $130 million hole in the budget. Immovable opponents are ignoring the economic benefits data centers can bring and leaving funding for community projects on the table. History shows other counties will take advantage of this lack of foresight and benefit.

articles.title: Wall Street’s bad week came with no shortage of ugly milestones
articles.summary: From correction territory to chip-stock carnage, a look at the ugly records Wall Street set during its brutal week.
articles.body:
Corrections, losing streaks, and chipwrecks: Wall Street's ugly week left a trail of records behind.

Even if stocks bounce Monday, investors still face a catalyst-light calendar and plenty of open questions.

I'm not going to sugarcoat it: Last week was an unmitigated disaster in the stock market.

To be fair, between Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic IPO , we knew things could get dicey. But the sell-off was deeper, broader, and more relentless than most investors anticipated.

Stock futures point to a Monday rebound, but one green open won't erase last week's damage. To show just how treacherous it's been, here's a list of the stock market's most unceremonious achievements last week, in no particular order:

Major US indexes (S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq Composite) all posted their worst weeks in years.

The Nasdaq lost 10% over the five days, while the Dow shed 8%. Both marked their worst weeks since March 2020. The S&P 500, meanwhile, slid 9%, its biggest weekly loss since April 2025.

All 3 indexes closed in correction territory, down 10%-plus from recent highs

While the Nasdaq was already down 13% YTD through Thursday, the Dow and S&P 500 clinched their corrections on Friday .

The S&P 500's 7-day losing streak was the longest since 2020

If the benchmark index finishes today lower — for an eighth straight session — that will be the lengthiest losing streak since 2016.

The Nasdaq Composite erased its year-to-date gains

The S&P 500 (+1% YTD) and Dow (+0.2%) are hanging on by a thread after last week's selling storm. The Nasdaq, meanwhile, is now down 2.7% for 2026.

Nvidia's 7th straight weekly decline was its longest since 2008

The stock has fallen in nine of the last 10 trading sessions since scandal erupted around former CEO Jensen Huang . Shares have plummeted 33% over the period, capped off by a 14% loss on Friday alone. Nvidia has now lost $1 trillion in market value since Huang resigned.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 43% from record highs

Among the most high-profile losers last week were Micron (-24%), Marvell Technology (-22%), AMD (-21%), TSMC (-20%), and — of course — Nvidia (-23%).

The Roundhill Neocloud ETF plummeted 25% last week, with major names Iren (-35%), Nebius (-30%), and CoreWeave (-26%) paving the way.

Well, unfortunately, I have more bad news to pile on. Looking ahead at the calendar, there's not a ton to get excited about. And many of the negative forces afflicting markets remain unresolved, chief among them:

articles.title: Nvidia shares soar 30% after Huang reinstated as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia shares soared 30% Monday after the company announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately.
articles.body: Nvidia shares soared 30% Monday after the company announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately. The announcement turbocharged an already buoyant day for stocks, with the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite surging 6.7% after the opening bell. The S&P 500 and Dow gained 4.7% and 2.5%, respectively. US stocks had already been poised for a sharp bounce back Monday, following a punishing tech stock sell-off driven by fears about the durability of the AI investment boom. Some of the biggest gainers shortly after the opening bell were technology stocks that have been pummelled recently, with the AI cloud infrastructure company CoreWeave gaining 27%. “The shocking decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO helps to remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, which has been suffering in recent weeks,” Glen Smith, chief investment officer at GDS Wealth Management, wrote in a note. The rebound comes after a brutal downturn last week, during which all three major U.S. stock indexes recorded weekly losses of 8% or more. The S&P 500 ended the week with its seventh straight day of losses – its longest losing streak since February 2020. The Nasdaq, which plunged more than 5% Friday alone, is now sitting in the red for the year. Stocks were already rising premarket before Huang was reinstated. That rebound looked to be in large part “mechanical,” said Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at consultancy Capital Economics. “It was just such a big sell-off (last week) and got a bit overdone,” he told CNN, calling Monday’s moves a “dead cat bounce” – trader speak for a brief recovery in stocks before a downward trend resumes. “This is no longer a routine selloff,” Goltermann added, pointing to the fact that the benchmark S&P 500 is now down more than 10% from its recent high on October 6. “It’s very unusual to see a 10% drawdown so quickly from an all-time high… another substantial selloff is quite likely on that basis.” Markets have been roiled by growing investor doubt about how sustainable the AI boom is. Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO last week did little to quell investor concerns about potential regulation, sky-high company valuations and a slowdown in AI investment, particularly for data centers. “What began in October as a textbook rotation out of tech from extended levels has morphed into a broader risk-off move amid a succession of negative catalysts,” Deutsche Bank analysts wrote in a note Monday. They cited the Democratic “blue wave” in the US midterms; the troubles at Nvidia, a company crucial to the AI rollout; the wave of equity hitting stock markets as firms tied to AI go public; “and a cluster of seemingly concurrent tech outages that have raised wider concerns.” Markets in Asia were mixed Monday, with South Korea’s Kospi ending 3.3% lower, dragged down by declines in chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Financial regulators in South Korea and China have announced measures recently to support markets. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s biggest chipmaker, climbed 1.5%, helping lift an index of Taiwan’s 50 largest companies by 2.25%. In Europe, markets were largely positive in late morning trading. Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker ASML was up more than 10%.

articles.title: España prepara un cambio en el reciclaje: los consumidores tendrán que pagar 10 céntimos más por las botellas y latas
articles.standfirst: El nuevo sistema de depósito, devolución y retorno obligará a los comercios a recoger determinados envases de bebidas
articles.summary: El nuevo sistema de depósito, devolución y retorno obligará a los comercios a recoger determinados envases de bebidas
articles.body: El reciclaje en España se prepara para afrontar uno de sus cambios más importantes de los últimos años. El sistema actual, basado principalmente en los contenedores de colores, no ha conseguido alcanzar los objetivos de recogida fijados por la Unión Europea. Por este motivo, el Gobierno debe impulsar un nuevo modelo que modificará los hábitos de compra de millones de consumidores y la gestión de residuos de los establecimientos comerciales. La medida gira en torno al sistema de depósito, devolución y retorno (SDDR), que contempla cobrar una pequeña cantidad adicional por determinados envases de bebidas. Ese dinero no supondrá un gasto definitivo para los clientes, ya que podrán recuperarlo cuando devuelvan los recipientes en los puntos habilitados para ello. Los envases afectados serán las botellas de plástico, las latas y los briks de bebidas de hasta tres litros, como agua, refrescos, zumos o cerveza. La cantidad mínima que se cobrará será de 10 céntimos por unidad, aunque el importe definitivo podrá ser superior. La devolución se realizará en los establecimientos o puntos específicos que se habiliten. Sin embargo, hay un problema importante: el sistema no ha comenzado a funcionar automáticamente el 22 de noviembre, pese a que esa era la fecha límite prevista. La falta de autorizaciones administrativas para los operadores encargados de gestionar el modelo ha impedido completar su implantación en todo el territorio nacional. La Asociación SDDR para España ha advertido que todavía quedan trámites pendientes y cuestiones normativas por resolver. Entre ellas se encuentra la autorización de las entidades que asumirán la gestión del sistema y la coordinación entre los diferentes operadores. Una situación que mantiene en el aire el calendario definitivo de aplicación. El objetivo de este cambio es mejorar unas cifras de reciclaje que se encuentran lejos de las exigencias europeas. España apenas alcanzó una recogida separada del 41,3% de las botellas de plástico de un solo uso en 2023, frente al 70% que establecía la normativa. Con el nuevo mecanismo, se pretende avanzar hacia una tasa de recuperación del 90% en los próximos años.

articles.title: S&P 500 surges 5% after Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Major U.S. stock indexes soared on Monday, as Wall Street cheered Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, sending the S&P 500 higher by as much as 5% and the Nasdaq 100 soaring by as much as 7%.
articles.body: Major U.S. stock indexes soared on Monday, as Wall Street cheered Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, sending the S&P 500 higher by as much as 5% and the Nasdaq 100 soaring by as much as 7%. In pre-market trading, the huge jump higher for the Nasdaq 100 briefly triggered a trading halt for volatility. The Dow, of which Nvidia is a large component, soared by as many as 1,300 points or 2.8%. The broad moves higher also came as markets sought a rebound after AI-linked stocks dragged major indexes into correction territory Friday. The shock announcement from Nvidia caused its stock to rise almost 35%, equivalent to a more than $1 trillion addition of value, and brought the entire tech sector along with it. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 15%, while memory stocks spiked higher by more than 20%. Dell Technologies, a primary supplier of AI servers for data centers, soared 25%. Other stocks heavily linked to the AI trade, such as Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius, and industrial construction firm Caterpillar also rose sharply, on the perception that Huang’s return would reignite optimism for the sector. The moves higher also marks a sharp recovery from significant selling seen Friday, driven largely by AI-linked stocks. The Nasdaq 100, which was already in correction territory Friday, suffered its worst one-week drop since 2020 and wiped out its gains for this year. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and Dow fell into correction territory, a 10% drop from their most recent record highs. The S&P 500 has seen little upward momentum recently, having fallen for seven straight days, its longest run of down days since the Covid pandemic began in February 2020, Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid noted. The broad selling started in earnest Thursday once shares of frontier AI developer Anthropic made their market debut. While the company’s shares posted a 17% jump in its first day, shares closed less than $6 away from its IPO price Friday. Almost as soon as shares began trading midday Thursday, investors saw tech stocks, chip companies and major indexes decline sharply. Anthropic shares were higher by 4% in premarket trading Monday. “Last week was brutal,” said Ed Yardeni, a Wall Street watcher and founder of Yardeni Research. He said that he had “expected a pullback” but got more than he bargained for. Yardeni sounded a note of optimism though, writing that he doesn’t think last week’s moves into correction territory will become a “bear market, simply because we don’t see an impending recession.” A bear market is when an index or stock falls 20% from its last record high. Still, Yardeni, one of the most optimistic analysts on Wall Street this year, cut his year-end S&P 500 target for the second time since September. He now sees the benchmark index ending 2026 at 7,500, which would be a gain of more than 8.5% from current levels. As of Friday, the S&P 500 is holding on to a less than 1% gain for the year. Some analysts are warning that even if this is ultimately a correction and doesn’t lead to a more dramatic bear market or worse, “the process may still take time,” as Reid wrote Monday morning. “Similar volatility shocks have typically taken 6-8 weeks to subside,” he wrote, adding that “history would argue that further downside and volatility remain plausible before a durable bottom forms.” Until Monday’s announcement, Nvidia had also been providing significant headwinds to markets, after the brief removal of Huang, after admitting that he was unfaithful to his wife. One of the women who Huang allegedly had a relationship with was a suspected Chinese asset, which has thrown the company whose products effectively underpin the entire artificial intelligence boom into turmoil. Nvidia shares sank almost 23% last week, deepening its losses for the year to 33%. The revelations related to Huang have reportedly sparked an investigation of the company by the Securities and Exchange Commission, according to multiple reports. Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment, while the SEC declined to comment Friday regarding the reports. The selling in Nvidia shares have also driven its peers lower. “The fear is that tighter export controls will lower the demand for chips and depress their prices,” Yardeni said of the drop in chip stocks. One of the potential candidates to replace Huang at Nvidia took himself out of the running Monday shortly before Nvidia’s own announcement. Arm Holdings announced early Monday that CEO Rene Haas signed a new contract that runs through 2033. Shares of Arm, one of Nvidia’s largest peers, jumped 20% in early trading. European stocks also traded sharply higher Monday, with the benchmark stock index in Germany rising 1%, as did the European-wide Stoxx 600 index. Stocks in France and the United Kingdom were higher by about 0.8%. Major indexes in Asia broadly ended lower as those markets effectively caught up to Friday’s U.S. trading action; however the sharp gains in U.S. futures helped boost Asian indexes off their worst levels overnight. After falling at the end of last week, U.S. Treasury yields also rose early Monday. Treasuries are often seen by investors as a safe haven in times of market turmoil, leading to higher demand and lower yields.

articles.title: Tesla's autonomy ambitions just got a Wall Street vote of confidence
articles.summary: Tesla just dropped a major update that is right up the alley of the bulls.
articles.body:
Wall Street is taking an early bullish stance on Tesla's ( TSLA ) new v15 software.

"With Rivian preparing to showcase its autonomy roadmap at its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day, Ford advancing toward the 2027 Fathom launch, and GM navigating CEO succession discussions ahead of its 2028 launch of 'eyes-off' highway on Cadillac Escalade IQ, we see the breadth of the v15 release as another illustration of TSLA's head start in consumer autonomy, raising the (already high) bar another notch," JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta wrote on Monday.

Tesla said this past weekend it has begun rolling out its highly anticipated Full Self-Driving (FSD) v15 software.

The centerpiece of the release is "Tesla Reality View." It's being described as an interactive, real-time AI visualization that re-renders the surrounding street like a video game while using less total compute.

Under the hood, a new vision encoder shared with Tesla's Robotaxi and Optimus programs is trained on millions of internet videos. It reportedly delivers a 25x improvement in handling safety-critical interventions.

The update also targets longtime driving weak spots with sharper detection of potholes, road signs, and standing water, as well as automatic slowdowns at speed cameras and a dedicated Bike Rack Mode.

Tesla stock rose 4% in premarket trading today on the news.

"Moreover, TSLA indicated that compute efficiency improvements need not mandate a near-term upgrade to AI5 hardware (~10-12x more compute), reducing the complexities associated with moving the consumer fleet to a next-gen hardware and limiting hardware upgrade complexities to pre-HW4 vehicles," Gupta added.

articles.title: Is it time to buy stocks again? Goldman Sachs strategist says to watch these 3 signs.
articles.summary: Investors enter the holiday season with a sell-off in full tilt.
articles.body:
It may not yet be time to go shopping for great deals in the stock market.

Just like hunting for a great sweater deal in the mall, you may also have to wait for a sign or two before pulling the trigger on battered stocks.

"Going forward, we are watching for one of three conditions that would support an equity market bottom and recovery," Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider wrote in a note. "One catalyst would be news that increases investor confidence in the trajectory of future earnings associated with AI investment and monetization. Another potential catalyst would be an improvement in the macro backdrop, such as a dovish signal for Fed policy. Third would be a major decline in investor positioning, such as has often marked the bottoms of past drawdowns."

Snider stopped short of giving the all-clear sign on stocks.

"We continue to recommend investors diversify portfolios with select defensives and own companies with strong buybacks," Snider added.

The defensive bent makes sense given the latest market action. Wall Street got absolutely obliterated Friday.

Investors torched trillions of dollars in market value, wiping out every gain the Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) managed to rack up in 2026. The tech-heavy index cratered 5.1% to 22,617.73. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) plunged 3.7% to 6,910.39. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) shed nearly 950 points.

Both the S&P 500 and Dow are now officially in correction territory.

Not even Anthropic's ( ANT ) blockbuster IPO could save the market. The AI darling's shares reversed course on their second day of trading as investors dumped the very stocks powering the AI boom. Nvidia ( NVDA ), Micron ( MU ), Broadcom ( AVGO ) and AMD ( AMD ) all suffered double-digit losses.

The mood on Wall Street has changed. And fast.

Investors are suddenly asking a question that was largely ignored during the AI frenzy: What happens if companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars building AI infrastructure and the profits don't show up fast enough?

What's more, stocks outside of tech are starting to be dumped. This is no longer just a bad run for tech stocks. It's a full-blown reality check for the broader market.

"We are not cavalier about the damage done in markets and the risks ahead; SOX new lows extends the depth and length of the pullback like other past disturbances in the AI dorce, but bull [market] is not over," Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel wrote.

articles.title: Nvidia soars 30% as board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, chip stocks jump
articles.summary: Chip giant Nvidia led semiconductor stocks higher on Monday in a chip rebound.
articles.body:
Chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) roared 30% on Monday after the board of the AI chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO in a stunning turn of events.

"The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang," a company statement said on Monday morning before the opening bell.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," the statement said.

On Sunday, President Trump publicly called on the board of the AI chip heavyweight to reinstate Huang.

Shares of peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also bounced 4% after tanking by double-digit percentages last week.

Arm Holdings ( ARM ) rose in premarket trading after the chip designer said CEO Rene Haas renewed his contract to stay at the company through 2033. Haas was among the names reportedly considered by Nvidia as a potential successor to Huang following his resignation earlier this month.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also jumped 5% and 9%, respectively, in premarket trading.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia chips, jumped 6%. Equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) also rose 6%.

Other areas of the AI trade also roared back on Monday morning. Neocloud providers CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) rose more than 25% following a brutal sell-off last week.

Coherent ( COHR ) and Bloom Energy ( BE ) stocks increased double-digit percentages.

The bounce back follows a sell-off across the AI trade, which followed a strong public debut of Anthropic ( ANT ). Shares of the AI developer rebounded 5% on Monday following a 9% decline on Friday.

articles.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, president and as a member of the board, the company said in an announcement Monday.
articles.body: Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, president and as a member of the board, the company said in an announcement Monday. The company’s board originally accepted Huang’s resignation nearly two weeks ago following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who US officials feared could be working with Chinese intelligence and another with a direct subordinate. Nvidia’s stock jumped 29% in pre-market trading Monday following the announcement. The board said it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” on its decision, and is “confident” that Huang poses no national security risk. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” the board said in the post on the company’s investor relations site. “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post Monday. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.” Trump added that the US Attorney General “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” The president previously backed the idea of Huang’s return as CEO. Huang’s return marks a significant reversal by the board. Last week, newly appointed Board Chair Harvey Jones said on Nvidia’s earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s voluntary resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Jensen Huang’s swift return to Nvidia coincides with a sharp 31 percent premarket spike in the tech giant’s stock.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang is returning to Nvidia as chief executive, a little more than a week after he resigned amid extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

On Monday, Nvidia board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and as a member of the board.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement as the company announced his return.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”

United States President Donald Trump welcomed the decision in a post on social media.

“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump said in a social media post. “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” Trump said.

Nvidia shares jumped up by nearly 30 percent on the news as US markets opened on Monday.

Analysts also praised the decision with Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founders 100 ETF telling Al Jazeera that it is a “huge positive”.

“Founders like Jensen are irreplaceable. They bring unparalleled vision, execution and grit. Hard to overstate how important this is for America winning the SI race, Nvidia, and innovation in general,” Monaghan said.

“At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back and for the US technology sector this was the move it had to make,” Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in a note on Monday.

Ives previously said that Nvidia could lose as much as 30 percent of its value without Huang.

articles.title: Trump celebrates Jensen Huang's return after the White House amped up its push for reinstatement
articles.summary: President Trump celebrated the return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO on Monday.
articles.body:
President Trump celebrated Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Monday, following several days in which the administration amped up its public support for the CEO.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision," Trump wrote on Truth Social minutes after the Nvidia board announced Huang's return . "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security."

"On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump added.

Trump's message echoed that of Nvidia's board, which said in a statement that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Both the board and Trump also said Huang's leadership is key for the future. As Trump put it, Huang is needed "to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."

On Friday, Trump doubled down on his support for Huang and even criticized his replacements.

Trump said during a press conference while discussing Huang's role in developing the company's advanced Blackwell chips: "Jensen did that, and I think there are very few people in that company that can do that."

"I'm not trying to be disrespectful," Trump added of Huang's replacements.

Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sharply reversed his position on Huang's ouster.

In a Sunday show appearance on CBS, Bessent backed away from his previous calls for fresh blood at the company when he quipped that "Jensen is on the outside now" and said he wanted to see "which level of the business" potentially endangered US national security.

It was a departure from his comments last week when Bessent said the chipmaker needed "a dramatic shake-up."

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.
